findings.title: Scalar flow_lift_factor is inverted: lifting water hotter RAISES COP (up to 2.02x), breaking batch parity
findings.claim: ThermalModel.flow_lift_factor returns max(0.25, carnot_ref/carnot_flow), which is >1 for every flow above the 35 degC reference, so compute_cop (valve plant, direct-plant curve) and compute_cop_dhw rise with flow/tank temperature on every climate, while the batch twin _batch_cop applies carnot_flow/carnot_ref.
findings.mechanism: The ratio of two Carnot COPs is inverted in the scalar law only. carnot_flow < carnot_ref above the reference, so ref/flow > 1: a 55 degC hot-water charge is priced at 1.34-1.61x the space COP instead of 0.62-0.75x, a throttled buffer at the tank temperature likewise, and the Carnot fraction of the priced COP exceeds 1 (a COP above the Carnot limit) on 21320 grid points in four of five climates. _batch_cop uses carnot_flow/carnot_ref, so scalar and batch disagree by up to 8.01 COP units on the same inputs.

findings.proposed_fix_scope: thermal_model.py ThermalModel.flow_lift_factor: invert the ratio to carnot_flow/carnot_ref (the batch twin's form); every DHW and valve golden fixture drifts.

findings.title: Measured defrost derate never derates: derate_from_duty adds duty x 1.5 and clamps to 1.0
findings.claim: defrost.derate_from_duty returns min(1, max(0.55, 1 + duty*1.5)) instead of the module's documented 1 - duty*DEFROST_LOSS_MULTIPLIER, so every measured duty in (0, 0.30] yields 1.0 and a fully trusted 20 % defrost duty leaves the frost-band COP unchanged (ratio 1.0, documented 0.70).
findings.mechanism: Sign error in the measured estimator. Because DERATE_MAX is 1.0 the result is pinned at 1.0; _decide hands the bucket to the measured estimator once duty_counts reaches DERATE_CONFIDENCE_SAMPLES, so on an install with a defrost flag the measured 1.0 also displaces any earned inferred derate: frost-band plans over-promise heat, the failure the module exists to stop.

findings.title: compressor_modulation=on_off is read as modulating: the declared on/off pump gets unclamped sub-p_min plans
findings.claim: thermal_model.declared_modulation maps COMPRESSOR_MODULATION_ON_OFF to True (modulating) instead of False, so a user declaring an on/off compressor gets clamp_planned_levels False on every set-point unit, and the solve prices 32 of 96 steps at levels in (0, p_min) the pump cannot run; auto on the same surface clamps (0 such steps).
findings.mechanism: Both explicit select values return True; the docstring and the options page say on_off -> False. Every reader inherits it: levels_clamped/duty_cycle_realizable (the plan's level law), learner_unmetered (the house learner's freeze) and probe_install(...).on_off. The explicit declaration is therefore weaker than leaving the key on auto.

On a flow/return set-point install the arbiter writes 55 degC (flow_heat_c) at full draw, while the priced space COP takes a flow lift only when flow_curve_cop_enabled is set (default off): the priced flow is not derived from the written set-point. The supply settles below the set-point by design (comment), so it is not shown to be wrong; recorded under priced-inputs-surface as 'modelled term, not surface-derived' for a seat measuring realised vs priced COP.
